Glioma.summary: Gliomas originate in the glial cells surrounding nerve cells in the brain.
Glioma.stage_info: Requires clinical MRI with contrast and biopsy for official WHO grading.
Glioma.next_steps: Schedule an urgent consultation with a neuro-oncologist.

Meningioma.summary: Meningiomas arise from the protective membranes surrounding the brain.
Meningioma.stage_info: Typically classified into Grade I (benign), Grade II, or Grade III.
Meningioma.next_steps: Consult a neurosurgeon to evaluate monitoring vs. intervention.

No Tumor.summary: No significant tumor mass detected in the evaluated brain MRI scan.
No Tumor.next_steps: If symptoms persist, follow up with a neurologist for further evaluation.

Pituitary.summary: Abnormal growth located in the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
Pituitary.stage_info: Evaluated based on hormonal activity and spatial pressure on optic nerves.
Pituitary.next_steps: Consult an endocrinologist and neurosurgeon for a comprehensive check.

Normal.summary: No clear radiographic features of osteoarthritis in the evaluated knee X-ray.
Normal.stage_info: This model outputs a coarse 3-way severity band, not a Kellgren-Lawrence grade.
Normal.next_steps: Maintain joint health through activity and weight management; review if pain persists.

Non Severe OA.summary: Radiographic features consistent with early to moderate osteoarthritic change.
Non Severe OA.stage_info: Coarse band covering doubtful through moderate disease; formal KL grading requires a radiologist.
Non Severe OA.next_steps: Consult an orthopaedic clinician about physiotherapy and pain management options.

Severe OA.summary: Features consistent with advanced osteoarthritis, such as marked joint space narrowing.
Severe OA.stage_info: Coarse band indicating advanced disease; surgical assessment is graded clinically, not by this tool.
Severe OA.next_steps: Seek prompt orthopaedic consultation to discuss surgical and non-surgical options.

Basal Cell Carcinoma (Cancer).summary: The most common form of skin cancer, arising from basal cells; rarely metastasises.
Basal Cell Carcinoma (Cancer).stage_info: Staging depends on lesion size, depth and location, confirmed only by biopsy.
Basal Cell Carcinoma (Cancer).next_steps: Arrange a dermatologist appointment for biopsy and excision planning.

Melanoma (Cancer).summary: Aggressive malignancy of pigment-producing melanocytes; early detection is critical.
Melanoma (Cancer).stage_info: Staged by Breslow thickness and spread, determined only by excisional biopsy.
Melanoma (Cancer).next_steps: Seek urgent dermatology assessment. Do not delay professional evaluation.

Nevus (Non-Cancerous).summary: Common mole formed by a benign cluster of melanocytes.
Nevus (Non-Cancerous).next_steps: Self-monitor using ABCDE criteria; report any change in size, colour or shape to a clinician.

No DR.summary: No visible diabetic retinopathy features in the evaluated fundus image.
No DR.stage_info: Grade 0 on the international DR severity scale.
No DR.next_steps: Continue routine annual diabetic eye screening and glycaemic control.

Mild Non-Proliferative DR.summary: Earliest stage, characterised by microaneurysms in the retinal vasculature.
Mild Non-Proliferative DR.next_steps: Confirm with an ophthalmologist and tighten blood glucose and blood pressure control.

Moderate Non-Proliferative DR.summary: More extensive microaneurysms, haemorrhages and hard exudates than mild disease.
Moderate Non-Proliferative DR.stage_info: Grade 2: more than microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR.
Moderate Non-Proliferative DR.next_steps: Ophthalmology review is recommended; monitoring interval typically shortens.

Severe Non-Proliferative DR.summary: Extensive haemorrhages, venous beading or intraretinal microvascular abnormalities.
Severe Non-Proliferative DR.stage_info: Grade 3: high risk of progression to proliferative disease.
Severe Non-Proliferative DR.next_steps: Prompt ophthalmology referral is strongly recommended.

Proliferative DR.summary: Advanced stage with neovascularisation, carrying significant risk of vision loss.
Proliferative DR.next_steps: Seek urgent ophthalmology care. Treatment may prevent irreversible vision loss.

Normal.summary: No radiographic evidence of pneumonia in the evaluated chest X-ray.
Normal.next_steps: If cough or fever persists, follow up with a clinician for further evaluation.

Pneumonia.summary: Radiographic features consistent with pneumonia - an inflammatory lung opacity, often consolidation or ground-glass change.
Pneumonia.stage_info: Severity (mild/moderate/severe) is assessed clinically using PSI/CURB-65; this screening tool flags presence only.
Pneumonia.next_steps: Seek clinical evaluation promptly. Management depends on severity, comorbidities, and local resistance patterns.
